name: MEMLENS
description: MEMLENS is a length-controlled multimodal benchmark for long-horizon conversational memory in vision-language models. It contains 789 questions instantiated at four context lengths (32K, 64K, 128K, and 256K tokens) and covers five memory abilities: Information Extraction (IE), Multi-Session Reasoning (MSR), Temporal Reasoning (TR), Knowledge Update (KU), and Answer Refusal (AR). Conversations are synthetically generated by a two-agent pipeline (GPT-5.1 as user and Gemini-3-Pro as assistant) and are interleaved with real images retrieved through iCrawler against general-purpose web image search. By construction, 80.4% of the questions are visually grounded; ablating evidence images on this subset collapses accuracy below 2% on two frontier VLMs. MEMLENS is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate long-context VLMs and memory-augmented agents under a unified, length-controlled protocol.

rai:dataLimitations: Conversations in MEMLENS are synthetically generated by a two-agent framework (GPT-5.1 as user, Gemini-3-Pro as assistant) and may exhibit generator-specific phrasing or rhetorical patterns that do not perfectly mirror naturalistic human typing or voicing dynamics; downstream conclusions about real-user behavior should be drawn with that caveat.

Images are retrieved from the open web via iCrawler and remain hosted at their source URLs; URLs may decay over time. The construction pipeline records the retrieval query and CLIP/SigLIP relevance threshold for every image so that semantically equivalent re-retrieval is possible, but exact-byte reproducibility cannot be guaranteed for arbitrarily old runs.
MEMLENS dialogues are written in English only. Multilingual generalization is out of scope.

The five-ability taxonomy (IE, MSR, TR, KU, AR) is by design narrow and does not exercise all phenomena that arise in conversational memory: in particular, MEMLENS does not cover audio, video, embodied perception, code execution, tool use, or long-horizon planning. Performance on MEMLENS should not be treated as a sufficient measure of general multimodal-assistant competence.
The 80.4% visually grounded subset and 19.6% text-only subset reflect the construction-time mix; users who reweight or filter the splits should report the resulting effective coverage.

Models that have seen MEMLENS questions or any subset thereof during training (data contamination) cannot be evaluated meaningfully on MEMLENS. We discourage inclusion of MEMLENS items in any training data.
rai:dataBiases: Image retrieval via iCrawler against general-purpose web image search inherits the demographic, geographic, topical, and language biases of the underlying search engines. Categories that are over-represented in commercial web search (e.g., Western consumer goods, English-language posters, North-American urban scenes) are also over-represented in MEMLENS.

The topic ontology that seeds question generation was authored by the dataset team and reflects their selection priors. Coverage of non-Western cultural artefacts, low-resource languages, indigenous knowledge, and underrepresented entities is therefore limited.

Synthetic dialogues are produced by frontier large language models (GPT-5.1, Gemini-3-Pro) whose pre-training distributions are themselves Western-centric, English-dominant, and Internet-skewed. These biases propagate into the conversation distribution: tone, register, named-entity coverage, and reasoning style all reflect frontier-LLM defaults.
Human-annotation auditing was performed by a small institutional cohort (computer-science-trained, English-fluent raters); their judgments may carry cohort-specific calibration biases.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: MEMLENS does not collect data from human subjects; the dialogues are between two AI agents and contain no real-user content.

Crawled images may incidentally depict identifiable persons (e.g., public figures in news photographs, performers, or athletes). The construction pipeline applies a negative-content filter that rejects candidates carrying watermarks, stock-photo logos, or copyright overlays at retrieval time, but it does NOT perform face detection or biometric scrubbing.

MEMLENS is released as a per-image URL manifest plus retrieval metadata, not as redistributed image bytes. This avoids creating a new redistribution channel for any sensitive content while still enabling reproducibility.
A takedown contact is provided in the project repository. Any image flagged to that contact is removed from the public manifest within seven days.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended use: standardized benchmarking of long-context multimodal conversational memory in vision-language models and memory-augmented agents at matched context lengths (32K, 64K, 128K, 256K tokens).
Suitable for: academic evaluation, model comparison across families and scales, ablation studies of memory mechanisms, error-mode and failure-case analysis, and agent-pipeline diagnostics.

Not intended for: training production systems (the synthetic-conversation distribution does not reflect real-user behavior); deriving deployment-grade safety claims; measuring real-user conversational dynamics or psychometric properties; biometric or surveillance applications.
Recommended evaluation use: testing only (held-out evaluation set). Inclusion of MEMLENS items in training data is explicitly discouraged.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impacts: by providing a length-controlled, multimodal joint benchmark for long-context VLMs and memory agents, MEMLENS accelerates progress on faithful, abstention-aware multimodal assistants, surfaces failure modes such as multi-session reasoning ceilings and abstention erosion under memory-management post-training, and enables fair comparison across model families and pipeline architectures. Negative impacts: like other public benchmarks, MEMLENS is at risk of being absorbed into training data (benchmark gaming) and of encoding the cultural and linguistic biases noted under rai:dataBiases. Mitigations: we release only the URL manifest and retrieval metadata (not bytes), tag a frozen v1.0.0 snapshot for reproducible evaluation, and explicitly discourage training-data inclusion in the dataset card; downstream comparisons should be interpreted within the documented scope, and authors using MEMLENS for cross-cultural or fairness claims should report the imposed reweighting.
rai:dataCollection: MEMLENS is constructed by a three-stage pipeline. (1) A topic ontology authored by the dataset team seeds question scenarios across the five memory abilities. (2) Images are retrieved through iCrawler against general-purpose web image search using topic-guided queries, then filtered by a negative-content classifier (watermark / stock-photo logo / copyright-overlay rejection) and CLIP and SigLIP relevance thresholds documented in the paper appendix. (3) For each surviving image-topic pair, GPT-5.1 plays the user and Gemini-3-Pro plays the assistant in a two-agent dialogue conditioned on the topic and image, producing multi-session conversations. Questions are then constructed against these conversations using ability-specific generators, instantiated at four context lengths (32K, 64K, 128K, 256K), and audited by human raters on a 484-question consensus subset before public release.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw inputs to the construction pipeline are: (a) the topic ontology authored by the dataset team; (b) iCrawler image-search results, recorded with source URL, retrieval query, retrieval timestamp, perceptual hash, BLIP-2 caption, and CLIP and SigLIP relevance scores; (c) GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro dialogue traces; (d) human-annotation worksheets used in the 484-question consensus audit. The raw artefacts are retained internally for reproducibility; the public release contains the structured derivative (per-image URL manifest, per-question JSON, prompt templates, and judge rubrics).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Per-image filtering: candidates are rejected if they carry watermarks, stock-photo logos, or copyright overlays; surviving candidates must pass CLIP and SigLIP relevance thresholds documented in the paper appendix.

Per-conversation filtering: structural validation enforces consistent turn count, image-token alignment between markup and image array, and evidence-session uniqueness (no two questions share the same source image).

Per-question filtering: judge-rubric tractability checks reject ill-posed items; for closed-form subtypes (7 of 9 reporting subtypes), deterministic-rule normalization is applied at scoring time so that judge variance is bounded.

Length controls: the same 789 questions are instantiated at 32K, 64K, 128K, and 256K tokens by varying the number of haystack sessions inserted around the evidence sessions; cross-modal token counting follows the protocol of MMLongBench.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioning: a frozen v1.0.0 snapshot is tagged at submission; subsequent revisions are released as new tags (v1.1.0, v2.0.0, ...) without rewriting historical tags, so that prior evaluation runs remain reproducible. Hosting: the dataset is hosted on a Hugging Face repository; an archival copy will be deposited on Zenodo with a permanent DOI at camera-ready. Maintenance commitment: the dataset will be maintained at least through NeurIPS 2027 (one full conference cycle beyond submission); extensions are announced on the dataset card. Decay handling: when an image source URL becomes unavailable, the recorded retrieval query and CLIP/SigLIP cutoff permit semantically equivalent re-retrieval through the same iCrawler pipeline. Takedown SLA: contact xrenaf@cse.ust.hk; any flagged image is removed from the public release within seven days.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human raters performed a 484-question consensus audit of the LLM-as-judge calls. Each item was independently rated by at least two raters following a written rubric (released alongside the dataset under judge_prompts/); disagreements were adjudicated by a third rater. Raters were calibrated on a 50-question training set before scoring production items. The judge rubric, calibration set, and inter-rater agreement statistics are documented in the paper appendix.
rai:annotatorDemographics: All raters held undergraduate or graduate degrees in computer science or a closely related field.
All raters were fluent English readers.

Raters were recruited from the dataset team's institutional research network; the cohort is small (single-digit raters) and demographically homogeneous, which is a known limitation noted under rai:dataLimitations and rai:dataBiases.
Raters were compensated at or above the local minimum wage applicable to research assistantships in their jurisdiction.

distribution.name: agent_subset_195.json
distribution.description: Indexing file (no QA payload) listing the 195 question_ids on which all seven memory-augmented agents are evaluated. Stratified-sampled from the full 789-question benchmark with seed=42 and intersected with available agent runs. Per paper Appendix G.2.

distribution.name: release_images
distribution.description: Local image cache used by the four dataset_*.json files. Contains 4,695 unique images (218.8 MB) referenced as the union of needles and haystack-session images across the 32K/64K/128K/256K variants. JPG/PNG/JPEG/WEBP. Image bytes are redistributed under the dataset license CC-BY-4.0 only insofar as the underlying source license permits redistribution; per-image source URLs and retrieval metadata are recorded separately so that re-retrieval is always possible. Files are organized under two folders only — haystack_images/ and needle_images/ — with randomized 12-character hex filenames (globally unique across both folders).

recordSet.name: questions
recordSet.description: MEMLENS questions. Schema is sourced from dataset_32k.json; the same 789 question_ids appear in dataset_64k.json, dataset_128k.json, and dataset_256k.json with longer haystack sessions.

field.name: question_id
field.description: Stable string identifier for the question; identical across the four context-length variants.

field.name: question_type
field.description: One of the five memory abilities: Information Extraction (IE), Multi-Session Reasoning (MSR), Temporal Reasoning (TR), Knowledge Update (KU), Answer Refusal (AR).

field.name: question
field.description: The natural-language question posed to the model.

field.name: answer
field.description: The reference answer used by the deterministic and LLM-as-judge scoring stages.

field.name: question_date
field.description: Timestamp string of the question turn (e.g. '2024/05/31 (Fri) 07:58').

field.name: haystack_dates
field.description: Per-session date metadata (used by Temporal Reasoning items).

field.name: haystack_session_ids
field.description: Per-session identifiers for each haystack session. The full nested haystack_sessions structure (list of list of conversation turn dicts) is available in the dataset_32k.json FileObject and is intentionally not surfaced here as a flat record field because mlcroissant cannot represent deeply nested objects in a single column.

field.name: answer_session_ids
field.description: Subset of haystack_session_ids containing the evidence for the answer; used for analysis but not provided to the model under evaluation.
